title: From the Editor — The Frontier Ahead

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Three powers share one frontier. When the Green Corridor opens, Naomi Sol guides a freighter of families toward a future they thought out of reach. A Shard cutter shadows them. Commodore Ella Venn sends the Fleet to protect the passage—an act of rescue to some, a claim of power to others.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Naomi wants her passengers to arrive with their choices intact. Ella must decide where protection ends and command begins. At Black Drift, Abby, Billie, and Tessa prepare another raid. The cargo could feed their families; Fleet expansion is turning old allies against each other.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Rex Fleet is about the people caught between survival, security, and home.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: As routes reopen, neighbors become strangers, rivals become uneasy allies,

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: and every choice changes who gets to move—and who is left behind.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Fast routes fail. Worlds lose contact.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: People build lives across a slower, divided frontier.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: New passages reconnect distant communities—and reopen old rivalries.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Yes, it’s AI. Why? Because it was fun to put together. I wanted to imagine people with competing needs, put them on a frontier full of choices, and see what happened. Thanks for coming along.

dialogueInline.speaker: DISPLAY
dialogueInline.text: REX FLEET ACADEMY: REACH AND RESOLVE

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A new generation enters the Fleet Academy to study history, doctrine, science, and navigation. But classroom rules meet real lives in the field.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Before the corridors reopened, generations grew up cut off. Follow the people who survived the collapse, formed new loyalties, and built futures in its long aftermath.

title: From the Editor — After the Rescue

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Mercy of Dawn reaches Auric, but a safe landing is only the beginning. Naomi has brought families through the fire; now Halev must find them shelter in a city already short on heat and medicine. Every open berth belongs to someone’s life, and every choice leaves a neighbor carrying the cost.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Venn risks her career to save the passengers, then refuses to turn rescue into authority over the people she saved. Richard and Paul keep fighting for their family and the strangers beside them. Tess helps across a battle line, while Abby and Billie face a rupture that friendship alone cannot mend. What does protection mean when the emergency is over?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric’s Crown Ring was built for comfort. Its empty apartments are not empty histories: doors, family belongings, failing heaters, and the people newly sheltered there all make competing claims on the same home.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric saved the ship. Now its survivors have to find a place in the city—and a way to live beside the people already there.

title: From the Editor — A Home Is Not a Berth

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A HOME IS NOT A BERTH

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric’s crisis has no clean villain and no easy room to spare. A returning family wants its apartment back; refugees need warmth tonight. Halev has to govern people whose claims are real, while Naomi insists that a temporary berth cannot become a permanent answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Richard and Paul put names and testimony to the choices that left Tal Corvus families without heat or medicine. Abby risks her standing to protect civilians; Billie and Tess discover how far fear can carry a trusted friend. And as Venn faces judgment, the people she rescued are still living with the consequences. When does a rescue become a promise—and who gets to keep it?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The fast Green Corridor brings more than ships. It accelerates migration, trade, and pressure on housing, so Auric’s old shortage becomes a frontier-wide argument about who belongs.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The next evacuation window is open. Families are ready to run, but every escort has a different idea of what protection should cost.

title: From the Editor — The Third Window

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At Tal Corvus, families do not get an abstract debate about freedom. They get one departure window, a child drawing the ships she hopes will come, and a choice about who will stand between them and the blockade.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Abby tries to set a boundary without claiming command of every Shard captain. Tess holds the departure mouth in Gravefire while Deka brings Thunderbreak's shields alongside; neither commands the other's ship. Naomi reads the danger in Jex’s warning and keeps the civilian ships moving. Even Pike, drawn first to the camera, crosses the line to save a stranded tug. The families make it through—but the cost follows them home.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A corridor window is brief and shared. Civilian pilots, Fleet escorts, and independent Shard crews must agree on timing long enough to get people through, even when none agrees who should lead.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The food arrives short, the routes are exposed, and Billie’s desperate attack has put the next relief run in danger.

title: From the Editor — The Cost of a Signal

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Jex makes route information public because people cannot cross safely on rumors. That choice helps civilian pilots find an open window—and gives raiders the same advantage. When Billie turns desperation into an attack on a relief freighter, the price is counted in lost crates, damaged ships, and families waiting at the ration door.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Naomi trusts a hand-drawn correction because it gets people to food. Tess puts Gravefire between the freighter and Ashfang, though her ship is already hurt. Billie withdraws, but the harm remains. This is a frontier where doing the useful thing can expose someone else to danger—and where people still choose to share what little arrives.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A route bulletin is more than a line on a map. Its timing can save a freighter, feed a neighborhood, expose a convoy, or give a captain leverage over people with no other way through.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Two narrow windows could move food and medicine through the blockade. Seven Shard captains will have to decide whose orders they follow.

title: From the Editor — Seven Captains Choose

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric’s missing food is still missing. The first convoy reaches the other side with a damaged mast, and the medical ships are not yet home. But at the Gate, seven Shard captains turn their weapons away one by one. No speech can make that choice for them; each accepts the risk to their own command.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Abby and Tess split the work instead of making a show of loyalty. Naomi flies the exposed route. Deka refuses to take credit for the Shard captains’ decision. Billie makes her own choice to shield Gravefire without joining the rebellion. The blockade opens without a battle, but Tal Corvus holds a new mystery in its walls. What changes when cooperation becomes an act of courage—and what waits in the corridor?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Gate is a crossing, a chokepoint, and a place where communities negotiate who gets through. A safe window needs more than a clear reading: it needs people willing to hold their fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The corridor looks safe on every instrument. Then the survey crew sees a second ship where no ship can be.

title: From the Editor — The Shape of an Echo

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Calm Corridor gives the survey crew a problem no one can shoot away. A ship appears where it should not, readings remain ordinary, and every synchronized correction seems to teach the echo what the convoy will do next.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Jia keeps measuring. Naomi trusts an untidy manual course. Tess puts the civilians ahead of the mystery, even when the mirrored Gravefire is impossible to ignore. The convoy survives by breaking formation rather than forcing perfect order. Then the Fear Mask turns one frightening image into a story of certainty. How do you keep people safe when the danger is real, but the explanation is still out of reach?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Reciprocal-field corridors depend on stable timing. In the Calm Corridor, synchronized ships create a pattern the echoes can follow; changing course becomes a human decision as much as a technical one.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At Shardfall, Tess faces Oren Pike in a witnessed captains’ challenge. The market is hungry, and the result will not fill a single ration bin.

title: From the Editor — The Price of Standing

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tess wins the challenge, but victory does not heal her arm or feed Veil Market. Pike is a capable opponent, and the witnesses see both her skill and the cost of the fight. Two captains choose to leave Raid’s muster; Raid answers by freezing their berths.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: While the duel holds the crowd’s attention, Naomi opens a safer second line at the ration door. Venn keeps Fleet power from turning Shard politics into an excuse for intervention. Abby accepts that each captain has to choose for themselves. What does a public victory change when the people waiting for food still have to get through the day?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A Shard captains’ challenge is witnessed because standing belongs to a community, not a single commander. Winning can change who listens; it cannot erase repair debts, hunger, or the choice each captain makes afterward.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Veil Market is hungry, Jex’s reserves are exposed, and someone has decided he should not live to open them.

title: From the Editor — What a Ledger Cannot Feed

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Jex opens his stores while the market burns, then gives up the freight access he once kept for himself. Food moves; the crowd eases; the fire still reaches his warehouse. His records begin to show a paid hand behind the attack and the diversions, but evidence cannot undo a shortage or make every honest buyer whole.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Naomi follows the trail without turning hunger into a conspiracy story. Sera asks for medical help without inviting an armed occupation. Venn finds a slower route that can keep aid moving. Jex gives up the secrecy of his deals, while protecting the hidden paths Tali may still need. Can a man repair trust when the same network that made him valuable also helped put people at risk?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Veil Market runs on bonds, storehouses, and routes people can actually use. When a barrier blocks the road, ownership means little to a family trying to reach food or a medic.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The records point to Shatterforge. Families are evacuating, the vents are locked, and Abby is going in.

title: From the Editor — The Last Minute at Shatterforge

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Shatterforge’s families live beneath the vents that keep their homes survivable. When the Fear Mask locks them, Tess opens a manual release and Abby holds Scythe over the exhaust so the skiffs can clear. Venn must choose who gets the last shield. The ships escape; Scythe disappears in the furnace bloom, and no one can say what happened to Abby.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Jex publishes the payment trail and his own part in it. Billie refuses an order to obstruct the departures. Pike’s bid to be seen nearly costs lives. The people reach shelter, but Abby is unaccounted for and the outward search stays open. How long can a rescue hold when every second asks someone else to risk their ship?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Shatterforge’s vents are part of daily life: heat, shelter, and a route out when things go wrong. Locking them turns a familiar home into a trap, and opening them again requires trust between people who do not share a flag.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric Gate is the next battlefield. Every faction will have to decide whether the civilian road stays open.

title: From the Editor — The Road Through the Battle

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Auric Gate is full of people before the battle begins. Venn keeps a lane open even when it weakens her formation. Naomi and Halev commit the Verge to keeping the crossing usable. Tess guides civilians through with Gravefire itself when the markers fail.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Abby returns with survivors and turns her bloc toward the civilian route. Billie draws a line she once could not hold. Pike chooses spectacle over safety until the cost becomes impossible to ignore. When synchronized fire feeds the Gate’s strange echoes, the answer comes from restraint shared across factions. No one wins cleanly. The road stays open—and people get through.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Gate carries more than ships. It carries schedules, food, families, and the trust that each side will leave a lane clear. When the road becomes a weapon, keeping it usable is its own kind of victory.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Now the ceasefire has to become rules. Billie brings the question the negotiators have avoided: who gets to decide when civilians move?

title: From the Editor — End of the First Run

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: When we started building Rex Fleet, the idea was much smaller than the universe it eventually demanded.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The starting point was the corridors: if civilization depends on a network of routes through dangerous space, somebody has to maintain them, defend them, map them and decide who gets to use them. From there came the Fleet, the Verge and the Shards—not simply as opposing factions, but as people with very different relationships to the same roads.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That gave us the world. The characters changed the book.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Tess, Abby, Naomi, Venn, Jex, Billie and the rest gradually stopped feeling like pieces positioned around a political conflict and started pulling the story in their own directions. Some relationships became more important than we expected. Characters who seemed destined for one role refused to stay there. A story that began with fleets and borders increasingly became about what people do when the institution they belong to no longer gives them an adequate answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Rift changed too. Early on, it was primarily the environment through which these people traveled. By the time we reached the Calm Corridor and the Mirror Star, it had become something much stranger. We still know more about what the Rift can do than the characters do—but not nearly enough to make it comfortable.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Making these twelve issues also taught us what Rex Fleet itself wants to be. It can hold battleships and refugee skiffs, political arguments and engineering problems, strange physics, marketplaces, old grudges, bad jokes and people trying to get dinner through a checkpoint. The enormous things work better when the ordinary things remain visible underneath them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That is the part we want to keep exploring.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: This issue closes the first major Rex Fleet story, but it does not close the universe. There are ships we have barely visited, regions we have only named, histories that have only been hinted at, and parts of the Lattice that nobody in this book has seen.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Most importantly, there are still stories we want to tell with these people.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Thank you for reading all the way to the end of the first run—and for giving us the chance to find out what Rex Fleet could become.
